title: Intro to Up Strums: Pattern 1 and Pattern 2 for Beginners
summary: In this beginner-friendly lesson, JustinGuitar introduces the first strumming pattern that includes an up strum after beat 2, showing how to count and execute it with a muted guitar neck and a pendulum-like forearm motion. He emphasizes slow, repetitive practice to develop a smooth, automated rhythm, explains how the up strum interacts with the beat (including the non-full-string nature of the up stroke), and offers practical guidance on staying in time even if chord changes falter. A second pattern adds a second up strum within the bar, followed by a discussion of tempo, relaxed technique, and the importance of repetition. The video foreshadows the most common pattern, nicknamed “Old Faithful,” and suggests applying these patterns to simple chords like A minor and E minor, with a reminder to practice rhythm (not just chord changes) and to use the Beginner Song Course app for pacing in time.

sections.description: Justin demonstrates the first strumming pattern that adds an up strum after beat 2, translating the stroke sequence into D D U D D. He shows how to count the measures (1...2 and 3...4) and explains that the up strum does not hit all strings. The segment emphasizes a relaxed, pendulum-like forearm motion and practicing slowly until the pattern can be performed evenly and in time.
